cards.text: Picture it, baker. Israel hasn't crossed the Jordan River yet, and the land God promised is waiting on the other side. Moses, Israel's leader, stands up with the elders of Israel and tells the people, "Keep all the commandments I am giving you today."
Then he gets specific. On the very day they cross the Jordan, they set up large stones and coat them with plaster. Kind of like icing a sugar cookie so the letters show up.

cards.question: Moses wants those big stones coated with plaster so something can go on them. What?

answers.text: All the words of this law
The names of the twelve tribes
The story of the river crossing

cards.question: Once Israel crosses the Jordan, the plastered stones go up on Mount ___.

cards.text: And it's not just stones with writing. They're to build an altar there too, an altar of stones to the LORD their God.

cards.question: Moses tells Israel to shape the stones for that altar with iron tools.

cards.text: Uncut stones only, and on that altar they offer burnt offerings to the LORD. So a cookie stamper would be USELESS on Mount Ebal. Shaping things is my WHOLE job, friend!

cards.question: When Israel sacrifices peace offerings on Mount Ebal, they eat them and ___ in the presence of the LORD.

cards.text: Then Moses comes back to those stones: write all the words of this law, and write them distinctly. Clear letters. No blurry stamps. Trust me, baker, I stamped blurry for YEARS, and nobody wants a blurry law.
Now Moses and the Levitical priests speak up, and this time it's to all Israel.

cards.question: What's the first thing Moses and the Levitical priests tell all Israel to do?

cards.text: A whole nation going quiet at once so they can listen. I have NEVER seen a group chat pull that off. Never. Not once.

cards.question: Moses and the priests tell Israel what they've become this day. What is it?

answers.text: The people of the LORD their God
A kingdom with its own king
Free to go their own way

cards.question: Because Israel is now the LORD's people, Moses and the priests say they shall obey His voice and follow His commandments.

cards.text: That same day, Moses gives the tribes their spots for after the crossing. Six tribes stand on Mount Gerizim: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph and Benjamin.

cards.question: What are the six tribes on Mount Gerizim there to do?

cards.text: The other six stand on Mount Ebal: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan and Naphtali. Twelve tribes, two mountains, six and six. Somebody put REAL thought into this seating chart.

cards.question: The six tribes on Mount Ebal are there to bless the people too.

cards.text: Then the Levites get the loud part. They proclaim to every Israelite in a loud voice. Mags would've LOVED this job.
First up: cursed is the man who makes a carved idol or molten image and sets it up in secret.

cards.question: After the Levites call out the curse on the secret idol, what are all the people to say?

cards.text: And they say it after every single curse. Twelve curses. Twelve Amens. A whole nation agreeing out loud, and I can't get my ovens to agree on ONE temperature.

cards.question: The next curse falls on whoever dishonors his father or mother.
Then a curse about land: cursed is he who moves his neighbor's ___ stone.

cards.text: Moving your neighbor's boundary stone. That's scooting the fence over a foot and hoping nobody notices. Somebody ALWAYS notices, friend.

cards.question: One curse is about a blind man. What does the cursed person do to him?

answers.text: Lets him wander in the road
Turns him away at the gate

cards.question: Next, cursed is he who withholds ___ from the foreigner, the fatherless or the widow.

cards.text: Then come four curses that draw hard lines around family and marriage: no sleeping with your father's wife, your sister or your mother-in-law, and no lying with any animal.

cards.question: Then a curse on the man who strikes down his neighbor in ___.
The next curse is on someone who kills an innocent person. What's behind it?
The last curse is only on the priests who don't put the words of this law into practice.

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave the two mountains for now. Moses isn't done preaching, friend. Not even close.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'fast' contradicts the question's own setup. The question says 'they eat them and ___', and eating and fasting can't both be true, so the baker can rule it out without reasoning about the passage.

rule.text: Wrong answers for what someone does or says only need to be believable.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: 'Then Moses comes back...' / 'Clear letters.' / 'No blurry stamps.' / 'Trust me, baker...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card says 'this time it's to all Israel', which implies the earlier words in 27:1 were spoken to a narrower audience. In 27:1 the audience is 'the people'. What actually changes in 27:9 is who is speaking (the Levitical priests instead of the elders), not who is listening.

rule.text: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing new from the passage. It restates the answer to card 11 (be silent and listen) only to set up a group chat joke. It also has three sentences.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The card says 'A whole nation going quiet at once', presenting the nation's silence as something that happened. In 27:9 'Be silent, O Israel' is only a command. The text never says the people went quiet.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The answers don't match each other. Two are noun phrases ('The people of the LORD their God', 'A kingdom with its own king'), but 'Free to go their own way' is a different kind of answer. The right answer is also the only one that sounds like the Bible ('the LORD their God'), so it stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone.

findings.problem: The setup 'Then a curse about land' rules out both wrong answers before the baker reasons about anything. An 'altar' stone and a 'grinding' stone aren't about land, so only 'boundary' fits.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing new from the passage. It restates the boundary stone curse just answered on card 10 only to set up a fence joke. It also has three sentences.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The card says these are 'four curses that draw hard lines around family and marriage', but one of the four (27:21, lying with any animal) has nothing to do with family or marriage.

rule.text: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The four sexual curses (27:20-23) are put together on one story card with no choice card. The walkthrough says key laws and teaching are not long stretches and get story cards and choice cards like anything else, and that a story card with more than two things happening should be split. The audience rules also say the content is for adults, kids can still play, and it must always stay clean.
findings.question: How should sexual-content laws like Deuteronomy 27:20-23 be handled? Is one summary story card with no choice card allowed for them, or should they be split and given choice cards like the other curses?
